hook.content: Imagine you have 4 yummy cookies on your plate. You eat 1 cookie for a snack. How many cookies are left on your plate now?

bigIdea.statement: Subtraction means taking away some objects from a group to find out how many are left.
bigIdea.whyItMatters: Knowing how to take away helps you share toys, figure out how many snacks are left, and solve everyday puzzles!

curatorBrief.title: Adventures in Taking Away!
curatorBrief.intent: Introduce young kindergarten learners to the concept of subtraction through playful stories of taking away objects from small groups (within 5 to 10) and discovering how many are left. Introduce the minus sign (-) as 'take away' and the equals sign (=) as 'shows how many are left'.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Demonstrate taking away objects from a small group to see what remains [apply]

components.title: Act Out: Taking Away!
components.intent: Guide kindergarteners to act out taking away items (such as birds flying off a fence or apples being picked) using numbers within 5. Students manipulate the objects to see how many remain.

components.title: Ten-Frame Take-Away
components.intent: Use a ten-frame with counters (within 5-10) to physically or visually take away counters, having students count and say aloud the number of remaining counters.

components.title: Snack Subtraction Hands-On Activity
components.intent: Provide a fun caregiver-guided screen-free activity where students count a small bowl of 5 crackers or grapes, take some away to eat, and tell how many are left.

objectiveBlocks.objectiveText: Identify the minus sign and the equals sign in a simple take-away sentence [identify]

components.title: Meet the Minus Sign and Equals Sign
components.intent: Introduce and define the minus sign (-) as the symbol meaning 'take away' and the equals sign (=) as the symbol meaning 'is' or 'how many are left' in basic horizontal subtraction sentences like 4 - 1 = 3.

components.title: Build a Take-Away Sentence
components.intent: Allow students to place number and symbol tiles into simple subtraction sentences (e.g., placing the '-' between quantities and '=' before the result), solidifying the role and appearance of each sign.

components.title: Spoken Subtraction Sentences
components.intent: Present simple subtraction sentences within 5 (e.g., 3 - 1 = 2) with voice prompts from the tutor, asking the child to recognize the minus and equals sign and speak the resulting remaining count.

finalAssessment.title: Subtraction Explorer Check!
finalAssessment.intent: Assess both objectives: asking students to determine how many objects remain when some are removed from a set, and identifying the minus sign (-) and equals sign (=) in a simple number sentence.

data.title: Snack Subtraction: The Case of the Disappearing Treats
data.subject: Math
data.overview: Turn everyday snack time into an exciting math adventure! Count out five tasty treats, physically take some away to eat, and discover how subtraction tells the story of what is left over.
learningObjectives: Count up to five concrete objects using one-to-one correspondence.
Demonstrate subtraction by physically removing items from a group of 5.
Verbally state subtraction story problems using foundational math words like 'take away' and 'is left'.

steps.title: Wash and Set Up
steps.instruction: Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water, then place your plate on the table.
steps.tip: A flat surface keeps round snacks from rolling away!

steps.title: Count Your Starting Snacks
steps.instruction: Place your 5 snacks onto the plate in a straight line and touch each one as you count out loud from 1 to 5.

checkpoint.question: How many snacks do you have in your starting group?

steps.scienceNote: Lining up objects helps our eyes and fingers match each item to one number name.

steps.title: The First Take Away
steps.instruction: Pick up 1 snack from your plate, move it onto your napkin, and eat it!

checkpoint.question: You started with 5 and took away 1. How many snacks are left on your plate?

steps.scienceNote: Subtraction is the math word for taking something away from a group.

steps.title: Tell the Snack Story
steps.instruction: Say the whole math sentence aloud: '5 take away 1 leaves 4!'
steps.tip: Using fingers to show 5 and then tucking 1 finger down helps reinforce the concept.

steps.title: The Mystery Snack Thief
steps.instruction: Close your eyes while your adult helper moves 2 snacks from the plate to your napkin, then open your eyes and count the remaining treats.

checkpoint.question: Did taking snacks away make your starting group larger or smaller?

steps.title: Subtract Down to Zero
steps.instruction: Count how many snacks remain on your plate, move all of them to your napkin to eat, and observe what is left.

checkpoint.question: When there are zero snacks left on your plate, does that mean the plate is empty?

reflectionPrompts.question: What happened to the total number of snacks on your plate every time you took one away?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Demonstrate subtraction by physically removing items from a group of 5.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about whether the number went up or down.

reflectionPrompts.question: If you have 4 crackers and you want 2 left, how many do you need to eat?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: State subtraction story problems using foundational math words.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Try hiding crackers with your hand until only 2 show.

reflectionPrompts.question: Where else in your day do you notice things being subtracted or taken away?
reflectionPrompts.connectionTo: Count concrete objects up to 5 with one-to-one correspondence.
reflectionPrompts.hint: Think about toys going into a bin, shoes coming off, or sips of water from a cup.

documentationPrompt.instruction: Take a photo of your plate showing your remaining snacks alongside your fingers holding up the number taken away.
documentationPrompt.suggestedCaption: I started with 5 snacks. I subtracted ___ and now I have ___ left!

extensions.title: Ten-Frame Snack Attack
extensions.description: Level up to subtracting within 10! Draw a 10-box grid on paper, place 10 snacks in the boxes, and subtract from 10.

extensions.title: Toy Animal Story Problems
extensions.description: Use small toy animals resting in a 'barn' box and act out animal subtraction stories when some wander out to the pasture.

safetyNotes: Adult helper recommended to supervise food preparation and activity.
Cut round foods like grapes or cherry tomatoes in half lengthwise to eliminate choking risks.
Wash hands thoroughly before and after handling edible materials.

data.description: Get ready to look at subtraction signs and speak your answers out loud!
data.gradeLevel: kindergarten students (ages 5-6) - Use clear language, relatable examples, foundational skills, and engaging visuals. Encourage exploration and basic problem-solving.

problems.question: What is 4 apples take away 1 apple?
problems.rationale: When you start with 4 apples and take 1 away, you have 3 apples left. Counting backward by one from 4 lands right on 3. This means 4 take away 1 equals 3.
problems.teachingNote: Use physical counters or fingers to model taking one away so students can see the quantity decrease by one.
successCriteria: Subtract 1 from a small group of up to 5 objects
Identify how many objects remain after taking one away
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.question: What number is two jumps back from four?
problems.rationale: Starting at 4 and jumping back 1 space lands on 3. Jumping back 1 more space lands on 2, so 4 take away 2 leaves 2. Counting backward helps us see subtraction in action.
problems.teachingNote: Have students place their finger on 4 and hop backward one tick at a time while counting aloud to reinforce the connection between subtraction and counting back.
successCriteria: Use a number line to subtract by jumping backward
Identify the result of subtracting 2 from 4
problems.subject: MATHEMATICS

problems.statement: True or false: The minus sign in this equation means we take away objects.
problems.rationale: True! The minus sign (-) tells us to take away or remove objects from a group, which makes our total number smaller. In this equation, starting with five and taking away two leaves us with three.
problems.teachingNote: Connect the minus sign to physical actions like eating a cookie or hiding toys so students can visualize subtraction.
successCriteria: Understand that the minus sign means taking away

problems.question: Which sign means take away when one balloon flies away?
problems.rationale: The minus sign shows subtraction or taking things away. When one balloon flies away from your group, we use a minus sign to show it is gone. The plus sign means putting things together instead.
problems.teachingNote: Reinforce the physical gesture of taking something away while pointing to the minus symbol. Connect the word 'minus' to real-life subtraction stories like losing or eating items.
successCriteria: Identify the minus symbol as the sign for taking away or subtraction.

detectedConstraints.description: obj2-di-math-facts prompts students to compute and vocalize differences rather than identifying the minus or equals signs.
The equals sign from the declared set (minus sign and equals sign) is never directly tested in assessment items.

coverage.summary: Objective 1 (taking away objects to see what remains) is fully supported with robust instruction and varied concrete assessment opportunities across story scenes, ten-frame tasks, and word problems. Objective 2 (identifying the minus sign and equals sign) is introduced well, but its assessment falls short: the equals sign is entirely omitted from direct identification items, and the dedicated practice block obj2-di-math-facts is off-target, testing mental fact computation instead of symbol identification.
